title: Concise integrity commit and recovery options brief
content:
Purpose:
Provide a short, customer-facing update and a set of recovery choices after the May 17th inference integrity deviation. This is intended for the status page + tenant-targeted messages and to seed postmortem language for account teams. Keep it action-oriented and explicit about options customers can select (replay, safe-mode, evidence bundle).

Audience: enterprise and mid-market tenants with production traffic in EU and us-west. Primary recipients: platform owners, customer SREs, product leads. Secondary: integration partners.

Snapshot (to publish on status page, 1–2 sentences):
On 2028-05-17 between 14:12–14:46 UTC we detected a small percentage of inference responses that did not match expected output signatures for some model variants in eu-west and us-west. A subset of tenants may observe truncated or semantically inconsistent outputs. We mitigated routing and KV-cache inconsistency by 14:55 UTC and continue to validate recovery.

What happened (concise for customers):
- Root cause (short): a race between cache-eviction and multi-variant routing after a rolling kernel update caused stale KV prefixes to be served for some requests. This produced a non-zero set of outputs with unexpectedly repeated prefixes or truncated structured fields.
- Scope: approx 0.6% of requests from 9 tenants across eu-west and us-west during the window. No successful authentication tokens were exposed; no data exfiltration observed.
- Impact: user-visible truncated replies or repeated sentence fragments; higher error count for structured output parses. Latency effects minimal for most requests.

Immediate mitigation and actions taken (what we did):
- Automatically rolled back the kernel change at 14:50 UTC and forced KV-cache invalidation across affected pools at 14:52 UTC.
- Disabled multi-variant routing policy that allowed legacy variants to be selected while the cache was in flux.
- Replayed warmup traffic and checksum-verified outputs for sampled request ids.
- Activated a tenant-specific safe-mode toggle for high-risk accounts to pin model variant and bypass cache until verification complete.
- Notified internal incident response; SREs are running a targeted audit for cache TTL mismatches.

Current status (what customers should know now):
- Service status: degraded -> mitigated. Core service is routing normally; we are still completing verification passes for tenanted replays.
- Verification: 100% of sampled replayed requests matched expected signatures after rollback and cache flush. Ongoing sampling until 2028-05-20 23:59 UTC.
- Customer-facing risk: low. If you observe inconsistent outputs after 15:00 UTC on 2028-05-17, use options below to request a replay/evidence package.

Customer choices and recovery options (explicit, actionable):
1) Opt-in replay (recommended for affected tenants wanting evidence):
   - What you get: a time-bounded replay of requests served during the incident window, checksums, and a delta report showing changed tokens/fields.
   - How to request: open a support ticket referencing JIRA-INC-1827 and include your tenant id(s) and desired time range (defaults to full window). Request form quick link: https://support.redwood.ai/replay-request
   - Timeline: we will provide an evidence bundle within 72 hours of request; priority escalation for enterprise contracts.

2) Tenant safe-mode (pin to a stable model variant + bypass cache):
   - Use case: customers who prefer immediate consistency by sacrificing short-term throughput gains from caching.
   - How to enable: contact your account team or run the API flag request safe_mode=true via console with tenant-scoped override. We can enable for you within 1 hour for enterprise accounts.

3) No action (monitor):
   - If you did not observe end-user impact, no action is required. We will continue sampling and notify you if additional evidence of impact is found.

Evidence and transparency package (what we include with a replay):
- Raw request ids (redacted tokens), server-side response checksums, diffed token sequences (human readable), routing trace (which variant served), cache TTL snapshot, operator timeline snippet.
- Note on privacy: we redact any tenant-supplied PII in replay artifacts; if you need full request payloads for legal/audit reasons, escalate with your account rep and legal team.

Operator notes and caveats (internal language we may surface as appendices):
- Known unknown: small probability that ultra-long-context requests (>32k) may have remaining edge-cases related to partial KV evictions; we are targeting a fix to ensure atomic eviction semantics in next kernel rollout.
- TODO: confirm whether the scaled-batcher heuristics contributed to the initial eviction order. Engineering owner: Marta R. (applied-ml).
- TODO: run a sweep for all dedicated pools with autoscale windows overlapping the deployment time range. SRE owner: Ethan C.

Suggested status page timeline (ops):
1) Immediate: publish the short snapshot above + link to this brief (this doc).
2) +24h: publish an intermediate verification update (sampling progress and any tenant replays queued).
3) Postmortem: include technical root cause, mitigations, and permanent remediation timeline. Target: 2028-05-26.

Communication snippets for account teams (short):
- High-trust customers: "We identified intermittent response integrity issues in a small fraction of requests on May 17. We've mitigated the root cause, validated replays, and can provide a replay bundle if you'd like."
- Low-friction notice: "We resolved a routing/cache issue on May 17 that affected a small number of responses. No action needed unless you see issues; contact support to request replays."

FAQ (quick):
Q: Will I be charged for replay or evidence bundles?
A: No, replay evidence bundles related to platform incidents are provided at no charge. If you request high-volume full payload exports for custom audits, we will coordinate with your account rep.

Q: Is customer data safe?
A: Yes. There is no evidence of data exfiltration. Replay bundles redact tenant PII by default.

Contact and escalation:
- Support portal: https://support.redwood.ai
- Incident lead: Priya Nambiar (pri@redwood.ai)
- Account escalation: your assigned AM or account-team@redwood.ai

Notes to self / drafting checklist (internal):
- Add verified sample output diff for 2 tenants to the evidence bundle before publishing intermediate update.
- Coordinate legal approval language for redaction statement.
- Confirm that statuspage incident tag and monitoring thresholds are updated to avoid duplicate alerts.

Appendix (optional for customers): operator timeline with timestamps, sample diffs (redacted), and list of affected pool ids.

-- end of draft --

Author notes: keep this doc short on the status page and link to a longer postmortem for customers who request full technical detail. We should avoid jargon on public-facing text; but include clear choices for replays and safe-mode so customers can take control quickly.
